text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian government files counter affidavit to a suit by detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola in which the politician is demanding the appointment of supreme court judges to enable it form a quorum hear his case.
- Oil share prices fall on Nigerian stock exchange as more than a million shares of four oil marketing firms are dumped in the market by investors.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha says in a message to the University of Lagos convocation ceremony that free education at all levels is not feasible now.
- Obafemi Awolowo University in southwestern Nigeria closed indefinitely following violent students demonstrations.
- Petrol supply to Lagos improves, easing a week-long fuel scarcity in the metropolis.
- African Development Bank appoints Nigerian Cyril Enweze, 54, vice-president for operations.
- Opposition NADECO group has again denied any involvement in the recent spate of bomb explosions in Nigeria.
- British negotiators ask for more time to consider new proposals from Nigeria on ending a mutual ban by the two countries on each other's aircraft.
- Shell oil firm refurbishes two hospitals in Delta state.
- Indian buyers signal intention to buy $30 million worth of cashew nuts from Nigeria.
- Twenty-six distressed banks which failed to meet a March 31 deadline to increase their capital base will be liquidated by June, says finance minister Anthony Ani.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha approves production sharing contracts for future oil exploration and production with multinational companies.
- A Chinese firm is to build a 2,240 megawatts thermal power station in Abuja, official sources say.
- Paint manufacturers are soon to announce a reduction in prices to woo consumers.
